case.case_title: Reddiar v. Van Houten and Others

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s freedom of association was infringed by the 1st respondent’s order barring him from entering the office premises without permission.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that the 1st respondent’s decision to prevent him from entering the office premises was motivated by his trade union activities and thus violated his freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the Board office is not a public place and the freedom of association does not include the right to enter any place at any time for any purpose. The petitioner was on compulsory leave and had no duties to perform, so restricting his access was justified.
key_facts: Petitioner was placed on compulsory leave and barred from entering the Board office premises except with specific approval.
The petitioner was an active trade unionist and alleged discrimination based on this.
The Board office is a public corporation but not a public place with free access.
The petitioner did not seek permission to enter the office and be refused; he claimed an absolute right to access.
The application for redress was filed more than one month after the order barring entry.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that the freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c) protects the right to form or join associations, not an unrestricted right to enter any premises at any time. The Board office is not a public place like a park and access can be restricted.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the petitioner was on compulsory leave with no duties, the 1st respondent’s decision to restrict his access was a reasonable administrative measure and did not infringe the freedom of association.
principles_established: Freedom of association does not include a right to enter any place at any time.
Public corporations’ offices are not public places with unrestricted access.
Restrictions on access to office premises for administrative reasons do not violate freedom of association.

outcome.holding: The court dismissed the claim that the petitioner’s freedom of association was infringed by the order barring him from entering the office premises.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: The petitioner’s claim of infringement of freedom of association was based on the order restricting his access to the office premises, which the court analyzed under Article 14(1)(c) to determine the scope of this freedom and whether it was violated.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court stated that the freedom of association is the freedom to form or join associations and not the freedom to enter any place at any time for any purpose. The Board office is not a public place and the petitioner had no absolute right to access it.
